title: QUIC RFC 9000 Initial Maximum Data Runtime Commit Verification
verification_method: Focused S18P2-0008 requirement-home tests over runtime transport-parameter commit and connection-level send-capacity enforcement, plus Release build, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, SpecTrace JSON validation, full Release test suite, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers the peer initial_max_data transport parameter becoming the runtime connection-level send limit for application data.
expected_result: The focused tests show that peer transport-parameter commit installs the initial_max_data value as ConnectionSendLimit and replaces any stale speculative connection send limit before application stream data can consume credit.
procedure: Run the focused S18P2-0008 and flow-control regression requirement-home filter.
Run the full Release test suite without rebuilding.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: Peer transport parameters are committed before application stream data is sent on the supported runtime path.
MAX_DATA frame handling remains a separate monotonic increase path after the initial transport-parameter value is committed.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim max_udp_payload_size receiver processing, max_ack_delay alarm-delay policy, broader Section 18.2 closure, public flow-control APIs, 0-RTT remembered transport-parameter validation, or hosted interop readiness.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-06. The Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the focused S18P2-0008 and flow-control regression filter passed 15/15, regenerated coverage triage marks REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S18P2-0008 trace_clean and reports 1,259 of 1,771 QUIC requirements trace-clean overall, core SpecTrace JSON validation passed for 439 artifacts, the full Release no-build suite passed 4,456/4,456, and git diff --check returned exit code 0 with line-ending warnings only.
